# Objective

Apply the four verified fifth-round review findings as one fix batch,
keeping the suite green and the documented policies in sync.

# Verified findings (all reproduced before fixing)

1. `build_read_structure` walked the raw record CIGAR: adjacent identical
   ops (`10M2I3I10M`) collapsed to the last write at a shared boundary —
   the merged pair lost 2 of 5 inserted bases.
2. SAM `=` SEQ shorthand (base identical to the reference) was treated
   literally: masked observations silently dropped as ineligible and the
   consensus degraded every such position to N@Q2 (merged NM=20 for one
   true SNV).
3. Output-collision checks compared `normpath(abspath)`, which does not
   resolve symlinks; `alias → real` let two outputs share one physical
   file — publication failed and left Parquet content at the BAM
   destination.
4. Coordinate ties hard-coded read number as leftmost in both pairing and
   merging, so colocated strand-swapped mates were rejected as
   `orientation_incompatible` while the read-number-swapped equivalents
   merged.

# Changes as executed

- `src/pairloom/alignment.py`: `build_read_structure` normalizes the
  record CIGAR before the walk; new `expand_reference_matches(record,
  contig, refcache)` resolves aligned `=` characters against the reference
  and restores `query_qualities` around the `query_sequence` assignment
  (pysam's setter drops them — found by the new regression test).
- `src/pairloom/pipeline.py`: `=` expansion in `_both_mapped` and
  `_adjust_single` right before discovery (no-op without `=`).
- `src/pairloom/pairing.py`: new `leftmost_is_read1(pos1, pos2, rev1,
  rev2, model)` — distinct starts by coordinate, ties by orientation model
  (fr: forward; rf: reverse; else read1); used by `select_pair`.
- `src/pairloom/merge.py`: `try_merge` uses the same helper.
- `src/pairloom/validate.py`: destination comparisons use
  `os.path.realpath`; `samefile` stays for existing paths.
- Tests: 4 regressions (adjacent-insertion merge, `=`-shorthand
  statistics/NM with positionally-built expectation, symlinked collision
  rejection, orientation-tie independence). Suite 147 → 151.
- README: symlink resolution, orientation tie rule, `=` expansion, test
  count. AGENTS.md: invariant 9 (CIGAR normalization + `=` expansion +
  the pysam qualities gotcha), test count.
- Benchmark: absolute numbers this session reflect a loaded machine
  (load average ~10); a same-load A/B against the stashed pre-batch code
  showed no code regression (post 8.7–9.4 s vs pre 9.0 s).

# Steps actually taken

1. Plan written; all four findings re-verified via the reproduction
   script.
2. Fixes applied; one file-corruption slip during test editing (a dropped
   newline after a class statement) was caught by collection and repaired.
3. Regressions added; two corrections during development: a test-side
   expectation bug (`.replace` matched the wrong position) and the real
   pysam qualities-drop gap found by the failing test.
4. Benchmark A/B under load; report, plan rewrite, audit, commits.

# Verification

- `pixi run test`: 151 passed (was 147; +4 regressions).
- Reproduction re-run: `10M5I10M` with all bases; NM=1 and one
  disagreement row for the SNV pair; symlink collision exits 2; both
  colocated strand variants merge.
- `pixi run lint` / `pixi run format`: clean.
- Benchmark: no code regression by same-load A/B (see the report's
  observation for the full table).

# Risks encountered

- The machine's load average (~10) initially masqueraded as a 25%
  performance regression; resolved by A/B measurement rather than
  assumption, with the context recorded in the committed report.
